walkthrough:
Differentiate $y = 1 - 4(2x + 1)^{-2}$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 0 - 4(-2)(2x + 1)^{-3}(2) = 16(2x + 1)^{-3} = \frac{16}{(2x + 1)^3}$$

Integrate $y$ with respect to $x$ using the reverse chain rule:
$$\int y\,dx = \int \left(1 - 4(2x + 1)^{-2}\right) dx = x - 4\left(\frac{(2x + 1)^{-1}}{-1 \times 2}\right) + c = x + 2(2x + 1)^{-1} + c = x + \frac{2}{2x + 1} + c$$

Determine the gradient of the normal line:
$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\frac{1}{2}$$

Write the equation of the normal line through $A\left(\frac{1}{2}, 0\right)$ and find its $y$-intercept $B$ ($x = 0$):
$$y - 0 = -\frac{1}{2}\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right) \implies y = -\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{1}{4}$$
$$\text{At } x = 0: \quad y = \frac{1}{4} \implies B = \left(0, \frac{1}{4}\right)$$

hints: Integrate curve from $0$ to $1/2$ to find area below $x$-axis: $\left[ x + \frac{2}{2x + 1} \right]_0^{1/2} = -\frac{1}{2} \implies \text{area} = \frac{1}{2}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle $OAB$ formed by the normal line, the $x$-axis, and the $y$-axis above $y = 0$:
$$\text{Area}_{\text{triangle}} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{16}$$

Evaluate the definite integral for the region between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x = 0$ to $x = \frac{1}{2}$:
$$\int_0^{1/2} y\,dx = \left[ x + \frac{2}{2x + 1} \right]_0^{1/2} = \left( \frac{1}{2} + \frac{2}{2} \right) - (0 + 2) = 1.5 - 2 = -0.5 = -\frac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{Area}_{\text{below axis}} = \left| -\frac{1}{2} \right| = \frac{1}{2}$$

Sum the triangular region above the axis and the curved region below the axis to obtain the total shaded area:
$$\text{Total Shaded Area} = \frac{1}{16} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1 + 8}{16} = \frac{9}{16} \quad (\approx 0.563)$$
